subject: Pricing and commit model for sustained 20B tokens/month
messages:
From: Anthony Burke <anthony.burke@edgecommerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick question on hosted rate for sustained high throughput

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latencies look great. We're modeling a plan that could hit ~20B generated tokens/month by mid-2027 across a mix of chat and batch summarize jobs.

Can you share the baseline hosted rate card for that scale and any discount schedule or commitment structures you offer? Specifically:
- Per-token baseline (input vs output split if you have it)
- Breakpoints for committed discounts (monthly/annual)
- Any credits for SLA or latency guarantees

Also, is there a recommended commit profile if we expect a ramp (1B -> 5B -> 20B over 9 months)?

Appreciate a high-level table — procurement will need it for our internal forecast.

Regards,
Anthony
Anthony Burke
Head of Applied ML, EdgeCommerce
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Anthony Burke <anthony.burke@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick question on hosted rate for sustained high throughput

Anthony — thanks for the note and for the time last week. High-level answers below; attaching a short rate table and a simple commit-credit model for your planning.

- Baseline hosted rate (approx): $0.0008 / output token; $0.0003 / input token (we publish exact per-model rates; this is representative).
- Breakpoints we commonly use: 0-500M, 500M-2B, 2B-10B, 10B+ (discounts increase at each tier).
- Commit structures: monthly rolling commitments or 12-month prepay; blended discounts for multi-year/consumption combos.
- SLA credits: available for enterprise (Dedicated/Private) — for Hosted we can include small SLA credit buckets tied to a 99.9% latency SLO at larger commitments.

For a ramp to 20B we typically propose a staged commit (3- or 4-slab) with true-ups quarterly so you don’t overcommit early but still capture volume pricing earlier in the ramp. See attached commit_credit_model.xlsx for a worked example.

If you want, Ben (cc'd) can share a tailor-made pricing table and a couple of contract samples.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick question on hosted rate for sustained high throughput

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Anthony's ask, attached are the ratecard & model I sent. EdgeCommerce looks like a good enterprise anchor: 20B/month potential, ramp profile attached.

Can we put together a pragmatic commercial we can present this week: propose a 12-month staged commit with quarterly true-ups, suggested blended per-token price target, and any SLA credit language we can offer on Hosted? Anthony explicitly wants an itemized table for procurement.

Ideal to include: recommended breakpoints, example invoice math (monthly true-up), and a note if Dedicated or a Hybrid routing approach materially changes the economics.

Thanks — Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Pricing <pricing-legal@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on hosted rate for sustained high throughput

Team — draft proposal below; attaching updated ratecard (redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf) and an example commit credit spreadsheet. Key points:

- Baseline (hosted): $0.0008 output / $0.0003 input (matches Naomi's note)
- Suggested staged-commit profile (12 months):
  * Q1: 2B committed (true-up monthly) — 7% discount off baseline
  * Q2: 5B committed — 12% discount off baseline
  * Q3: 8B committed — 18% discount off baseline
  * Q4: remaining to reach 20B — 25% discount for 10B+ slab
- Blended rate example: if they hit ramp schedule, blended output token rate ~ $0.00058 (worked example in spreadsheet).
- SLA credits for Hosted: up to 2% monthly credit for latency SLA misses at the 20B commitment tier (requires acceptance of data access logs for audit).

Notes/asks: procurement will push on annual prepay vs monthly true-up. If they want prepay, we can add an extra 3% discount across slabs. Also want to clarify refund/true-up mechanics in the contract (see pricing-legal on cc).

If this looks good, Naomi can present to Anthony.

Ben
VP, Commercial Pricing
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Anthony Burke <anthony.burke@edgecommerce.com>, EdgeCommerce Procurement <procurement@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: staged commit + blended rate example (EdgeCommerce)

Anthony / procurement team — attached are two artifacts: 1) a short ratecard pdf, and 2) a worked commit/true-up spreadsheet that maps the ramp you described to blended per-token economics. Highlights:

- Staged 12-month commit (Q1–Q4) as discussed — preserves ramp flexibility while delivering meaningful discounts early.
- Example blended output rate: $0.00058/token (if ramp proceeds as modeled).
- Prepay option: +3% off blended rate if paid upfront for 12 months.
- SLA credit: we can commit to a 99.9% latency SLO for prioritized routing; up to 2% invoice credit for any monthly SLA breach at the 20B commitment bracket (requires audit logs).

Next steps: procurement to confirm whether they prefer monthly true-up or 12-month prepay. If they opt to proceed, we'll share an initial commercial term sheet and a DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Naomi
From: Anthony Burke <anthony.burke@edgecommerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, EdgeCommerce Procurement <procurement@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged commit + blended rate example (EdgeCommerce)

Naomi — thanks, this is exactly what we need. Procurement has two quick asks before we move to terms:

1) Can you confirm the blended rate math assumes output-focused workloads (we had about 70% output tokens in the demo)?
2) We'd like the prepay option spelled out as an invoice schedule (they prefer a single annual invoice).

If you can confirm those two items and include a DocuSign link for a 12-month prepay with the +3% structure, we can take to our CFO and aim to sign next week.

—Anthony
